report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are well-defined and signed off, team has direct stack experience (React/Python/Django), but scope includes medium-complexity integrations (PagerDuty, email scheduling) and real-time data refresh that may require iterative validation with stakeholders.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to the existing customer analytics dashboard to eliminate manual report generation.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Customer Success team (15 people) and Sales team (25 people)
project_understanding.trigger: CSMs are spending 10 hours/week manually generating reports; leadership wants automated dashboards to reduce manual effort.
success_definition: CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes
90% of scheduled reports delivered on time
supporting_quotes: Customer success managers are spending 10 hours/week manually generating reports. Leadership wants automated dashboards.
Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to our existing customer analytics dashboard.
CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes; 90% of scheduled reports delivered on time; Alert response time < 1 hour

assumption_log.what: Email Service (A3) is an internal or third-party SMTP service with documented API and SLA; no custom email infrastructure build required.
assumption_log.why: Use case model shows Email Service as secondary actor in UC5 (Schedule Report Delivery). Brief specifies 'Email scheduling' as requirement but does not detail email provider. Standard practice for internal tools is to assume existing email service (SendGrid, AWS SES, or internal SMTP) rather than build custom.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Resource Planning) — assume existing shared services unless explicitly stated as build scope.
assumption_log.consequence: If email service does not exist or requires custom build, Phase 2 scope expands by 1–2 weeks; if SLA is undefined, scheduled report reliability metric (90% on-time) becomes unachievable without email service SLA commitment.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Reduces Phase 2 scope by ~40 hours; enables 90% on-time delivery metric. Risks: If email service is unavailable or undocumented, scheduled report feature fails; team must pivot to custom build or alternative provider.

assumption_log.what: PagerDuty integration scope is limited to webhook ingestion and alert routing; no custom PagerDuty escalation policy or incident management workflow build required.
assumption_log.why: Use case model shows PagerDuty as external actor in UC6 (Configure Alert) and UC7 (Receive Alert Notification). Brief specifies 'PagerDuty integration' but does not detail scope of integration (webhook only vs. full incident lifecycle management). Standard practice is to assume webhook-based alert delivery unless brief specifies custom escalation or on-call scheduling.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 (Scope Definition) — external system integrations default to documented API unless brief specifies custom workflow.
assumption_log.consequence: If PagerDuty integration requires custom escalation policy, on-call scheduling, or incident lifecycle management, Phase 2 scope expands by 1–2 weeks; alert response time metric (< 1 hour) may require PagerDuty SLA validation.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Reduces Phase 2 scope by ~30 hours; enables alert notification feature. Risks: If PagerDuty integration scope is broader than webhook ingestion, team must re-estimate and re-plan Phase 2.

assumption_log.what: Real-time data refresh (every 15 minutes) is achievable with existing PostgreSQL database and does not require data warehouse migration, streaming pipeline, or materialized view infrastructure.
assumption_log.why: Brief specifies 'Real-time data refresh (every 15 minutes)' and use case UC2 requires KPI widgets refreshed every 15 minutes. Brief does not specify data volume, query complexity, or current database performance. Standard practice for internal dashboards is to assume 15-minute refresh is achievable with polling or scheduled queries on existing database unless brief specifies high data volume or sub-minute latency requirement.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 (Schedule Development) — assume standard refresh cadence unless brief specifies real-time (< 1 minute) or high-volume streaming.
assumption_log.consequence: If data volume or query complexity prevents 15-minute refresh on PostgreSQL, team must architect data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) or streaming pipeline (Kafka, Fivetran), adding 3–4 weeks to Phase 2 and increasing budget by $10K–$20K.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Reduces Phase 2 scope by ~50 hours; enables real-time KPI widget feature. Risks: If database performance is poor or data volume is high, team must pivot to data warehouse or streaming architecture.

hard.technology_stack: Frontend: React; Backend: Python/Django; Database: PostgreSQL; Alerting: PagerDuty integration
hard.compliance: Must integrate with existing authentication (SSO); Data retention policy: 2 years

nfr.security: SSO authentication required; existing SSO provider integration (A5 in use case model)
nfr.performance: Custom report generation < 5 minutes; real-time data refresh every 15 minutes
